text:
maria: quick summary — ran FP8 kernel parity scan for Orion-20B on H100 and L40S pools. Enabled kernel on both pools, compared to GPTQ/AWQ baselines. short-ctx PPL delta small (+0.15-0.35) but longprefix (>2k) shows serious degradation (+~3.0 ppl) and occasional token-reuse loops in tail (~0.3% of requests).

maria: config used for canary:
```
canary:
  model: orion-20b-v1
  fp8_kernel: true
  precision_fallback_threshold: 0.4
  routing_policy: region_then_perf
  deploy_nodes: [h100-pool-2,l40s-pool-4]
```

maria: quick numbers (eval set mixes short/long prefixes):
- H100 short (<=512): baseline GPTQ 11.9 -> FP8 12.1
- L40S short: baseline 12.0 -> FP8 12.2
- H100 long (2k-4k): baseline 10.8 -> FP8 14.0 (repro across 3 runs)
- L40S long: baseline 11.1 -> FP8 15.3

ayesha: can you paste the smallest repro trace for the token-reuse loop? is this happening at generation time or in beam rescoring?

maria: happens during autoreg decode (greedy/top-p). sample snippet (masked for PII):

"token_trace": "...the user asked for X. the assistant said the user asked for X. the assistant said the user asked for X..."

maria: attached quick heap of runtime counters: kv_cache_misses spike on longprefix, runqueue_latency climbs, and we see tiling-eviction events on L40S around 78-85% runqueue.

dan: two suspects — activation scaling + tiling stride mismatch on L40S. if act scale is global it can saturate mantissa for long contexts and trigger numeric drift. also L40S kernel picks a different vector width for the GEMM path which changes accumulation order.

dan: try per-channel act scaling + force tiling stride to fixed. also lower concurrent_batch on L40S to avoid runqueue steal.

sam: AWQ vs GPTQ note: AWQ kept short-ctx ppl better in these runs but produced higher tail degeneration. GPTQ had slightly worse short-ctx but more stable longprefix. we should gate routing by workload: prefer AWQ for <512, GPTQ for >=2k, and FP8 only in short/medium after more checks.

zhang: observed an L40S-specific kernel path that uses 128-bit tile packer — with longprefix it ends up reordering reductions; result is tiny bias that accumulates across many tokens. lowering the micro-batch size reduces the accumulation window and mitigates. this is consistent with the 78-85% runqueue region Maria saw.

maria: reproduce command we used:
```bash
# run canary harness
python infra/canary/run.py --model orion-20b-v1 --pools h100-pool-2,l40s-pool-4 --fp8-kernel enable 
--evalset evals/longprefix_mixed.json --act-scale per_tensor
```

maria: logs and traces: s3://redwood-canaries/orion20b/3141592653/{h100,l40s}/trace-*.tar.gz

deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for orion-20b-v1 at 2026-03-20T15:03:21Z — 4 nodes healthy, 2 degraded (L40S), routing fallback active.

ayesha: can we get the eval harness to include overlapping prefix shifts (sliding window) to catch cumulative bias earlier?

dan: yes — add windows of 256 overlap, up to 3k total. also run with per_channel scaling + alternate tiling config.

sam: suggested quick AB plan: 1) baseline route (GPTQ), 2) AWQ short, GPTQ long, 3) FP8 gated short-only. small traffic (5%) for 24h with targeted logs for prefix>1k.

maria: next steps I propose:
- short term: disable FP8 on L40S for production routing, keep H100 FP8 off until we finish per-channel scaling and tiling fixes.
- mid term: re-run parity scans with per-channel act scaling & micro-batch <= 4 on L40S.
- add longprefix sliding-window eval (up to 3k) and tail-degeneration detector (repetition > 8 tokens).
- AB run for 48h with routing gating as Sam outlined.

zhang: agree. i'll open a kernel bug with repro and attach perf traces + compiler flags that produce the 128-bit packer path.

maria: thanks — assigning follow-ups: @zhang kernel bug, @dan eval harness edits, @sam AB config. I'll hold a brief sync tomorrow to prioritize. :thumbsup:
